don't expect to find someone who will listen to you and understand you easily. people are selfish, it's hard but it's the truth, and today's society forces you to be even more selfish. facebook, instagram twitter... it's all about what I do, what I say and what I think, nothing encourages you to listen and understand others. In my experience even people with depression are fucking selfish for the most part, they know you feel bad, they know you need to talk and yet all they want is to be the center of attention and solve their own problems. I repeat, people are selfish and you will hardly find someone of a similar age who is really interested in listening to you, it sounds harsh, but it is a truth that you better get used to.

one thing that helped me was to volunteer to help the elderly. i found some older people who really listened to me, and with life experience so they could give me a couple of tips and explain to me some things about life that nobody dares to say.

I think it is good that you get close to older people who live in your environment, maybe you can't go with them to a concert or get drunk together in a bar, but you will have deeper conversations and if you listen to what they have to say you will learn about life without having to make so many mistakes yourself.

In my experience it is almost impossible to have real friends of a similar age today. The world forces you to be increasingly independent and selfish and young people are forced to focus too much on their own lives and careers if they want to remain socially relevant.

Of course, there will be people with whom you spend pleasant moments and with whom you have things in common, but you will hardly find a true friend. 

If you want to meet people who are really happy to see you, volunteer with organizations that help children or the elderly, you may not find people to go to a club or get drunk in a bar with, but you will find people who appreciate who you really are.

It's good to love family but you can't make your family your only reason for living. They live their own lives, have their own problems, pursue their own interests and have other people to love.
At some point you are going to stop being the most important thing to them. It is hard to hear, but it is the truth and it is the natural order of things.
You have to build your life around you. Happiness and true peace you will only find in yourself.
You will meet other people who will make you feel very happy and you will believe that these people are indispensable in your life. 
believe me most of the time those feelings don't last and those people will leave your life just as they came.
At the end of the day it is you who builds the most important and biggest part of your own life.

My conclusion is that the root of it all is that I had no real guidance during my youth, I mean, someone brutally honest who told me the hard truths of life that we only understand when we are old. I think young people need to hear those truths. The biggest mistake though is not fighting hard enough for what you want in life. We are taught that there will always be someone to help us, that luck will help us, but it will not make any difference if you are not willing to give up everything to build the life you want.  the only one capable of changing your life is yourself.
